title: The catalog, rebuilt by full rescan
description:
## Parent

[Spec: yt-transcript — a Node CLI turning YouTube videos into Markdown transcripts](ytdlp-xmu)

## What to build

A **catalog** at `transcripts/README.md`: a Markdown table of every transcript on disk, derived
wholly from **frontmatter** so it cannot drift from what is actually there.

Two triggers, both required. **Automatically** after a successful single-video fetch, and
**explicitly** via `yt-transcript catalog` — a subcommand on the single entry point, not a flag and
not a second executable. Automatic-only goes stale the moment a transcript is deleted by hand, which
is exactly when an index starts lying; explicit-only makes the common path two commands.

A **rebuild is always a full rescan**, never an incremental append. That is what makes drift
structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely.

The scan rule is **"any `.md` with parseable frontmatter is a transcript"**, which excludes the
catalog itself as a side effect — it has no frontmatter — with no filename special case.

Five columns, in order: **Title** (linked to the transcript's relative path), **Channel**,
**Duration**, **Uploaded**, **Subtitles**. `url` and `fetched` are deliberately not surfaced;
`fetched` would churn a row on every re-fetch. Sort by `upload_date` **descending**, tie-break
`title` **ascending** — both immutable, so a re-fetch never reorders a row.

Above the table an `# Transcripts` heading, then a single line reading
`N transcripts, regenerated by yt-transcript catalog`. That note is load-bearing: the file is
derived, so anyone hand-editing it loses the edit and the file must say so.

A malformed transcript is **skipped with a warning naming the file and telling the user to
re-download it** — never silent, never fatal. One bad file must not cost the whole catalog.

**Derivability is the standing test for any future column:** computable from the seven frontmatter
keys plus the file path, or it does not belong.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A successful single-video fetch leaves the catalog matching what is on disk
- [ ] `yt-transcript catalog` rebuilds without fetching anything
- [ ] Deleting a transcript by hand and rebuilding removes exactly that row
- [ ] The catalog never lists itself
- [ ] Columns match the settled set and order, and each Title links to its transcript
- [ ] Rows sort by upload date descending, ties broken by title ascending
- [ ] A `|` in a title is escaped in the catalog cell only — frontmatter and filename untouched
- [ ] Zero transcripts yields the heading and the count line, and no table
- [ ] A transcript with unparseable or incomplete frontmatter is named in a warning and skipped, and the rest of the catalog is still written
- [ ] Covered at the catalog seam: `(array of { path, raw text }) -> { markdown, warnings }`, so the scan rule and the warning are both inside the tested boundary

## Blocked by

- One video becomes one transcript on disk

title: Failure behaviour and the retry ladder
description:
## Parent

[Spec: yt-transcript — a Node CLI turning YouTube videos into Markdown transcripts](ytdlp-xmu)

## What to build

Make every failure mode legible, and retry the one failure that is actually transient.

**The success test** is exit 0 **and** a non-empty subtitle file. Both halves are needed: a video
with no captions in the requested language exits **0**, says
`There are no subtitles for the requested languages`, and writes nothing.

**Classification needs no stderr parsing.** Measured directly: no captions exits 0, an HTTP 429
exits **1**. The exit code alone separates the permanent failure from the retryable one.

- **No usable subtitles at all** is a hard error: exit 1, no file written, no catalog rebuild. Inside
  a batch it is an ordinary failure-summary entry — permanent, not retried.
- **HTTP 429 is the one retried exception**: 3 attempts with 5s, 15s and 45s between them, reported
  as *rate-limited* and naming the video. Every other failure is permanent and not retried, because
  the no-retry rule was reasoned from permanence rather than convenience.
- **The message must not oversell "try again later."** The translation endpoint has been observed to
  refuse a session's very first request, and again after a four-minute cooldown, while native tracks
  succeeded in the same minute. It is a near-zero standing allowance, not a refilling quota — so the
  wording may say a later run *may* succeed and nothing stronger.
- **A rate-limited translated track is not distinguished from any other 429.** It cannot be: the
  pre-flight that would diagnose it was rejected by decision, so both are the same observable —
  non-zero exit, `HTTP Error 429`, no file. The user sees exit 1 and the rate-limited message.
  **There is no second exit code.**
- **The requested language is the output language, always.** No cross-language fallback; the
  frontmatter has nowhere to record one. The **original spoken language is never surfaced, never
  named in an error, and never suggested as a `--lang` value.**

`--lang <code>` selects the language, default `en`, matched **exactly** — `en` does not match
`en-US`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fetch that exits 0 but writes no subtitle file is treated as a failure, not a success
- [ ] No usable subtitles exits 1, writes no transcript, and triggers no catalog rebuild
- [ ] An HTTP 429 is retried 3 times with 5s / 15s / 45s waits before giving up
- [ ] A permanent failure is not retried
- [ ] Failures are classified from the exit code alone — no stderr text is parsed to decide
- [ ] The rate-limited message names the video and says a later run *may* succeed, nothing stronger
- [ ] No error message names or suggests the video's original spoken language
- [ ] `--lang` selects the language and matches exactly
- [ ] Exit codes are covered by tests, using recorded process outcomes rather than live network calls

## Blocked by

- Skeleton, target parsing, and a fetched subtitle track

Success is exit 0 plus a non-empty track; classification is exit-code-only; the 5s/15s/45s ladder retries the rate-limited case with injected waits. 77 tests pass. One deliberate divergence recorded in comments: with stderr parsing forbidden, every non-zero exit is necessarily treated as rate-limited.

   invocation plus 3 retries = 4 invocations. The invocation count is always derived as

   change.

   is the no-captions signal, **every non-zero exit is classified rate-limited and retried** — a
   private or deleted video included. The spec's "every other failure is permanent" is the
   *reasoning* behind the rule, not a distinction the code is allowed to draw. It is not a bug in

   attempt reads as success. Asserted by test.

- `fetchFailure({ exitCode, hasTrack, url, lang })` is the classification entry point if a batch

- The one-second inter-fetch delay, the single end-of-batch catalog rebuild and skip-set computation

title: Playlists and channels expand into batches
description:
## Parent

[Spec: yt-transcript — a Node CLI turning YouTube videos into Markdown transcripts](ytdlp-xmu)

## What to build

A playlist or channel URL **expands** into a **batch** of **fetches**. A fetch is still one video,
one invocation — a batch is many fetches, never one large one.

**Detection is purely syntactic**, matching how `yt-dlp` picks its extractor before any network
I/O.

- **`watch?v=...&list=...` means the video.** A deliberate divergence from `yt-dlp`'s own default,
  implemented by the `--no-playlist` already on every per-video invocation. **`--playlist` forces
  the batch reading** of such a URL.
- A bare `@handle` is rewritten to the channel's **Videos tab**; left alone, `yt-dlp` would expand
  it to Videos plus Shorts plus Live.
- **Expansion is its own invocation** — `--flat-playlist --simulate --print` over the playlist or
  channel URL — and the only one that reads a playlist. Its output is normalised to the settled
  canonical URL form, then each video is fetched by the ordinary per-video invocation.
- **Skipping is batch-only.** A single video URL still overwrites. A batch subtracts what
  `transcripts/` already holds, using the same full scan the catalog rebuild performs, and matching
  on the frontmatter `url` — **not** on the filename. **`--force` means exactly "ignore the skip
  set"**, nothing more.
- Failures **continue, collect, report**: the batch runs to the end, then names what failed, and the
  process exits non-zero if anything did. **Expansion failure is a hard error.** Zero videos, and a
  batch where everything was skipped, are **successes**.
- **No cap on batch size**, but a **one-second delay between fetches**, implemented in our own loop:
  every `yt-dlp` sleep flag acts inside a single invocation and so cannot help here.
- **One catalog rebuild at the end of the batch**, never one per video — per-video rebuilds would
  make a 200-video playlist quadratic.
- **Playlist provenance is not recorded.** The playlist is how you found the video, not what the
  video is, and recording it would fail the catalog's derivability test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A playlist URL fetches every video in it, one transcript each
- [ ] A channel URL and a bare `@handle` both resolve to that channel's videos
- [ ] `watch?v=...&list=...` fetches only the video
- [ ] `--playlist` on that same URL fetches the whole playlist
- [ ] Re-running a batch fetches nothing that is already on disk
- [ ] `--force` re-fetches everything in the batch and changes nothing else
- [ ] The skip set matches on frontmatter `url`, so a renamed transcript file is still recognised
- [ ] One failing video does not stop the batch; the run ends with a summary naming it
- [ ] The process exits non-zero when any fetch failed, and zero when all succeeded or all were skipped
- [ ] A batch that expands to zero videos is a success
- [ ] Expansion failure is a hard error
- [ ] Consecutive fetches are at least one second apart
- [ ] The catalog is rebuilt exactly once for the whole batch
- [ ] Skip-set computation is covered at its seam: `(expanded urls, existing urls, force) -> urls to fetch`

## Blocked by

- The catalog, rebuilt by full rescan
close_reason: Batches delivered and merged to feat/yt-transcript: syntactic detection via parseTarget, expansion as its own invocation, url-matched batch-only skipping, continue/collect/report with one-second spacing and a single end-of-batch rebuild. 154 tests pass. Expansion additionally verified live against a real 9-video playlist.

## Implementation report — ytdlp-xmu.6

Merged to `feat/yt-transcript`. `npm test` passes: **154 tests, 0 failures, 0.88s** — the batch's
one-second spacing and the retry ladder are both injected, so nothing sleeps for real.

Commits: `c6bbcea` feat: playlists and channels expand into batches;
`81c1be5` fix: a batch reports a failure in the same words a single fetch does;
`cd6a196` refactor: the batch roll-call says which failures are worth re-running.

### Files

New: `src/batch.js`, `src/batch-plan.js`, `tests/batch.test.js`, `tests/batch-plan.test.js`.
Changed: `src/ytdlp.js`, `src/catalog.js`, `src/catalog-store.js`, `src/cli.js` and their test files.
Untouched: the cleaning pipeline, the repository root, the fixtures' line endings.

### Seams and signatures

- **`src/batch-plan.js`** — the seam the ticket names, pure:
  `planBatch(expandedUrls, existingUrls, force = false) -> { toFetch, skipped }`. Order-preserving,
  de-dupes a video a playlist lists twice, and `skipped` names only videos *this* batch expanded to.
  `force` does exactly one thing: bypass the subtraction.
- **`src/batch.js`** — continue, collect, report, with the clock injected:
  `runBatch(urls, { fetchOne, lang, sleep, delayMs, onProgress, onRetry, onFailure }) -> Promise<{ fetched, failures }>`;
  `describeBatch({ fetched, skipped, failures }) -> { summary, failureLines }`; `FETCH_DELAY_MS = 1000`.
- **`src/ytdlp.js`** — expansion lives beside the other invocation rather than in a new module, so
  `run()`'s `sanitizeChildEnv`, `shell: false` and ENOENT mapping are not duplicated:
  `expandArgs({ url })`, `parseExpansion(stdout) -> string[]`, `expandPlaylist({ url, binary })`,
  `ExpansionError`.
- **`src/catalog.js`** — `scanTranscriptUrls(files) -> string[]`, sharing `renderCatalog`'s own
  frontmatter parse, so the skip set and the catalog cannot drift apart.
- **`src/catalog-store.js`** — `readExistingUrls({ dir })`; it and `rebuildCatalog` now share one
  private `readTranscriptFiles(dir)`.
- **`src/cli.js`** — deps grew to
  `{ preflight, fetchTranscript, rebuildCatalog, expandPlaylist, readExistingUrls, sleep }`;
  `--force` added to `parseArgs` and the usage text.

1. **Expansion prints `%(id)s`, not a URL**, and normalisation goes through `parseTarget` — the one
   place that knows the canonical form. `--js-runtimes node` is deliberately absent from the
   expansion: its rationale is subtitle extraction, and a flat listing runs no player JS.
2. **A listing row `parseTarget` cannot read is dropped, not fatal.** Losing a whole channel over one
   unplayable row is the worse failure.
3. **The rebuild is unconditional and exactly once**, including zero-video and all-skipped batches.
   "Exactly once" is only a testable claim if nothing can skip it.
4. **Exit code comes from failed fetches; rebuild *warnings* do not set it**, matching the
   single-video path — but a rebuild that *throws* does, and its message prints after the failure
   summary, never instead of it.
5. **`--force` on a single video is accepted as a no-op**, not rejected: a single video URL
   overwrites anyway, so it asks for what already happens. "Nothing more" cuts both ways.
6. **A non-`FetchError` escaping a fetch is still collected and the loop continues**, recorded with
   `failure: null`. Running to the end is the batch's contract; an uncaught surprise would discard
   every transcript already reported.
7. **The batch preflights `yt-dlp` before expanding**, since a batch spawns.
8. **Playlist provenance is recorded nowhere.** Frontmatter stays closed at seven keys.

**Spec axis found one real defect, fixed in `81c1be5`:** `describeBatch` truncated each failure to

strictly less than one hitting it outside. Failures are now reported in full as they happen via
`onFailure`, which is also what makes the closing roll-call's terseness honest.

It also named a coverage gap: the skip set's two halves were each pinned only against their own side.
Closed by a test where real `parseExpansion` output meets a real `renderFrontmatter`-written url
through `scanTranscriptUrls` — the drift it guards against is silent and total (nothing skips,
everything re-fetches, exit 0). The missing assertion that `--no-playlist` is on the per-video
invocation was added.

**Standards axis:** a stale `src/catalog.js` module header and three rationales restated verbatim
across files, both fixed; `planBatch`'s result key `fetch` renamed `toFetch` (it collided with the
glossary's **fetch** and shadowed the global); a four-positional-parameter clump folded into one
object.

### Verified live by the orchestrator, outside the seams

`expandPlaylist` was run against a real 9-video playlist on the merged branch. `expandArgs` emits
`--flat-playlist --simulate --print %(id)s` as settled, and `parseExpansion` returned **9 canonical
`https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>` URLs**. This retires the silent-failure mode flagged below:
had real `--print` output not matched the assumed shape, expansion would have returned `[]` and the
batch would have succeeded with zero videos and exit 0.

### What ytdlp-xmu.7 must know

1. **Watch for a silent zero, not for an error**, if anything about expansion changes — though the
   live check above has now exercised it end to end.
2. **The eight acceptance fetches need no `--force`.** They are single video URLs, which overwrite
   regardless; skipping is batch-only.
3. **Do not hand-add frontmatter to `transcripts/README.md`** — it is excluded from the scan
   precisely because it has none.
4. **Nothing has been deleted from the repository root.** All 13 fixtures are in `tests/fixtures/`
   and the suite passes, so the ticket's "confirm before deleting" precondition is satisfiable now.
5. The `import.meta.main` entry-guard gap on Node 22 and the Windows `.cmd`/`.bat` yt-dlp shim
   limitation are both still open and unchanged.
6. A batch with several failing videos is slow: each failing video costs up to 65s of retry ladder
   plus 1s spacing.
